description: PAM authentication attempt for a sudo command
sample:
Log Name:      audit/USER
Source:        sudo (pam_unix)
Event ID:      1100 (USER_AUTH)
Level:         Notice
Host:          web01.prod.example.org
Description:
A user's password was checked while starting a sudo session.
type=USER_AUTH msg=audit(1732200011.221:48812): pid=18432 uid=1000 auid=1000 ses=12
subj=unconfined_u:unconfined_r:unconfined_t:s0-s0:c0.c1023
msg='op=PAM:authentication grantors=pam_unix acct="jsmith" exe="/usr/bin/sudo"
hostname=? addr=? terminal=/dev/pts/3 res=success'
reference: See PAM result codes reference table for the full set of `res=`/failure values.

hostname=? addr=? terminal=/dev/pts/1 res=failed'

msg='op=PAM:accounting grantors=pam_unix,pam_faillock acct="mchen" exe="/usr/sbin/sshd"
hostname=203.0.113.44 addr=203.0.113.44 terminal=ssh res=success'

description: Account temporarily locked after repeated failed logins (pam_faillock)
sample:
Log Name:      audit/USER
Source:        login (pam_faillock)
Event ID:      1101 (USER_ACCT)
Level:         Warning
Host:          bastion02.prod.example.org
Description:
Account validation failed: the account is locked out by pam_faillock after too many
consecutive failed login attempts.
type=USER_ACCT msg=audit(1732201355.410:49101): pid=9013 uid=0 auid=4294967295 ses=4294967295
subj=unconfined_u:unconfined_r:unconfined_t:s0-s0:c0.c1023
msg='op=PAM:accounting grantors=? acct="rjones" exe="/usr/bin/login"
hostname=? addr=198.51.100.23 terminal=/dev/tty1 res=failed'
reference: faillock --user rjones shows the individual failed attempts that triggered the lock.

hostname=192.0.2.15 addr=192.0.2.15 terminal=ssh res=failed'
reference: See PAM result codes reference table.

description: Controlling TTY recorded for a sudo session
sample:
Log Name:      audit/USER
Source:        sudo (pam_unix)
Event ID:      1124 (USER_TTY)
Level:         Information
Host:          web01.prod.example.org
Description:
The keystrokes/TTY device associated with a privileged session were recorded for
later replay (e.g. with `aureport --tty`).
type=USER_TTY msg=audit(1732200011.230:48813): pid=18432 uid=1000 auid=1000 ses=12
subj=unconfined_u:unconfined_r:unconfined_t:s0-s0:c0.c1023
msg='tty=/dev/pts/3 data=6C730D0A comm="sudo"'
reference: `data` is the hex-encoded keystrokes; decode with `aureport --tty` or `ausearch --tty`.

description: A user ran a command as root (or another user) via sudo
sample:
Log Name:      audit/USER
Source:        sudo
Event ID:      1123 (USER_CMD)
Level:         Notice
Host:          db01.prod.example.org
Description:
sudo logged the exact command that was authorized and about to be run.
type=USER_CMD msg=audit(1732200012.500:48814): pid=18432 uid=1000 auid=1000 ses=12
subj=unconfined_u:unconfined_r:unconfined_t:s0-s0:c0.c1023
msg='cwd="/home/jsmith" cmd=737973746D6374 6C20726573746172742073736864
terminal=/dev/pts/3 res=success'
reference: cmd= is hex-encoded; `systemctl restart sshd` in this sample decodes to "systemctl restart sshd".

description: A process explicitly set its capability set via capset(2)
sample:
Log Name:      audit/SYSCALL
Source:        kernel (capset)
Event ID:      1322 (CAPSET)
Level:         Notice
Host:          web01.prod.example.org
Description:
A process changed its own effective/permitted/inheritable capability sets — worth
reviewing whenever the resulting set includes something like CAP_SYS_ADMIN outside
of a known service's expected startup sequence.
type=CAPSET msg=audit(1732205000.100:50210): pid=22190 comm="nginx"
cap_pi=0 cap_pp=3fffffffff cap_pe=3fffffffff cap_pa=0
frontier=400000000000
reference: See the Linux capabilities reference table for what each bit in cap_pe/cap_pp/cap_pi means.

Log Name:      audit/USER
Source:        useradd
Event ID:      1114 (ADD_USER)
Level:         Notice
Host:          web01.prod.example.org

A new user account was added to the local account database.
type=ADD_USER msg=audit(1732205500.200:50300): pid=25011 uid=0 auid=1000 ses=12

msg='op=adduser id=1010 exe="/usr/sbin/useradd" hostname=? addr=? terminal=/dev/pts/3

description: A user was added to a privileged group (e.g. sudo/wheel)
sample:
Log Name:      audit/USER
Source:        usermod
Event ID:      1132 (GRP_MGMT)
Level:         Warning
Host:          web01.prod.example.org
Description:
A user's group membership was changed — here, added to the `sudo` group, granting
them the ability to run privileged commands. The single highest-value account-
management event to alert on in this catalogue.
type=GRP_MGMT msg=audit(1732206400.200:50440): pid=25170 uid=0 auid=1000 ses=12
subj=unconfined_u:unconfined_r:unconfined_t:s0-s0:c0.c1023
msg='op=add-supplementary-group grp=sudo acct="rjones" exe="/usr/sbin/usermod"
hostname=? addr=? terminal=/dev/pts/3 res=success'

description: A new process was created via execve() (paired with EXECVE/CWD/PROCTITLE/EOE)
sample:
Log Name:      audit/SYSCALL
Source:        kernel (execve)
Event ID:      1300 (SYSCALL)
Level:         Information
Host:          db01.prod.example.org
Description:
The kernel-level record of a monitored system call — here, execve(), the Linux
analogue of Windows Event ID 4688 (process creation). Always emitted together with
an EXECVE record (arguments), a CWD record, a PROCTITLE record, and an EOE record
closing the group, all sharing the same audit(...) timestamp:serial pair.
type=SYSCALL msg=audit(1732207000.300:50600): arch=c000003e syscall=59 success=yes
exit=0 a0=55a1e2f3c0d0 a1=55a1e2f3c120 a2=55a1e2f3c1a0 a3=0 items=2 ppid=18432
pid=25400 auid=1000 uid=0 gid=0 euid=0 suid=0 fsuid=0 egid=0 sgid=0 fsgid=0 tty=pts3
ses=12 comm="systemctl" exe="/usr/bin/systemctl"
subj=unconfined_u:unconfined_r:unconfined_t:s0-s0:c0.c1023 key="exec"
reference: Companion records: EXECVE (arguments), PROCTITLE (raw cmdline), EOE (end marker).

description: The argument list passed to an audited execve() call
sample:
Log Name:      audit/SYSCALL
Source:        kernel (execve)
Event ID:      1309 (EXECVE)
Level:         Information
Host:          db01.prod.example.org
Description:
Companion record to SYSCALL: the argv[] array the process was launched with.
type=EXECVE msg=audit(1732207000.300:50600): argc=3 a0="systemctl" a1="restart"
a2="sshd"
reference: Shares the audit(...) timestamp:serial with its parent SYSCALL record.

description: The full raw command line of an audited process, as one string
sample:
Log Name:      audit/SYSCALL
Source:        kernel (execve)
Event ID:      1327 (PROCTITLE)
Level:         Information
Host:          db01.prod.example.org
Description:
Companion record to SYSCALL: /proc/pid/cmdline captured at exec time, hex-encoded.
type=PROCTITLE msg=audit(1732207000.300:50600):
proctitle=73797374656D6374 6C007265737461727400737368 64
reference: Hex-decodes to "systemctl restart sshd" — decode with `ausearch -i` rather than by hand.

description: Marks the end of a multi-record audit event
sample:
Log Name:      audit/SYSCALL
Source:        kernel (audit)
Event ID:      1320 (EOE)
Level:         Information
Host:          db01.prod.example.org
Description:
Closes out a group of related records (e.g. SYSCALL+EXECVE+CWD+PROCTITLE) that
share the same audit(...) timestamp:serial pair — tools like ausearch use this to
know a logical "event" is complete.
type=EOE msg=audit(1732207000.300:50600):

description: A file under an audit watch (-w) was read
sample:
Log Name:      audit/SYSCALL
Source:        kernel (fs watch)
Event ID:      1302 (PATH)
Level:         Notice
Host:          db01.prod.example.org
Description:
A path matched by an auditctl -w watch rule was accessed — here, a read of
/etc/shadow outside of any known password-management tool.
type=PATH msg=audit(1732207500.400:50700): item=0 name="/etc/shadow" inode=131099
dev=fd:01 mode=0100640 ouid=0 ogid=42 rdev=00:00
objtype=NORMAL key="sensitive_read"
reference: Paired with a SYSCALL record giving the process (pid/comm/exe) that made the access.

description: A kernel module was loaded
sample:
Log Name:      audit/SYSCALL
Source:        kernel (module loader)
Event ID:      1330 (KERN_MODULE)
Level:         Warning
Host:          web01.prod.example.org
Description:
A kernel module was inserted via init_module()/finit_module() — legitimate for
hardware/driver support, but also a classic rootkit persistence technique, so
unexpected modules on a server are worth immediate review.
type=KERN_MODULE msg=audit(1732208000.500:50800): name="xt_nat"
reference: Pair with a SYSCALL record (comm/exe/pid) to see which process loaded it.

description: An audit rule was added or removed
sample:
Log Name:      audit/SYSCALL
Source:        auditctl
Event ID:      1305 (CONFIG_CHANGE)
Level:         Notice
Host:          web01.prod.example.org
Description:
The running audit rule set was changed — a watch, syscall rule, or filter was
added or removed.
type=CONFIG_CHANGE msg=audit(1732208200.600:50820): auid=1000 ses=12
subj=unconfined_u:unconfined_r:unconfined_t:s0-s0:c0.c1023
op=add_rule key="identity" list=4 res=1

description: Auditing was disabled at the kernel level (auditctl -e 0)
sample:
Log Name:      audit/SYSCALL
Source:        auditctl
Event ID:      1305 (CONFIG_CHANGE)
Level:         Critical
Host:          web01.prod.example.org
Description:
The kernel audit subsystem itself was disabled — the direct Linux analogue of
Windows Event ID 1102 "The audit log was cleared". After this point nothing is
being recorded until it's re-enabled; forward this event off-box immediately.
type=CONFIG_CHANGE msg=audit(1732208300.700:50830): auid=0 ses=99
subj=unconfined_u:unconfined_r:unconfined_t:s0-s0:c0.c1023
op=set audit_enabled=0 old=1 auid=0 ses=99 res=1
reference: If this wasn't an authorized maintenance window, treat it as an active incident.

description: The system booted
sample:
Log Name:      audit/USER
Source:        kernel (init)
Event ID:      1127 (SYSTEM_BOOT)
Level:         Information
Host:          web01.prod.example.org
Description:
Recorded once auditd is up during early boot, confirming when the audit trail for
this boot cycle began.
type=SYSTEM_BOOT msg=audit(1732190000.000:1): pid=1 uid=0 auid=4294967295
subj=kernel msg='comm="systemd" res=success'

description: The system is shutting down
sample:
Log Name:      audit/USER
Source:        kernel (init)
Event ID:      1128 (SYSTEM_SHUTDOWN)
Level:         Information
Host:          web01.prod.example.org
Description:
Recorded as systemd tears the system down — the last audit record before the
trail picks back up at the next SYSTEM_BOOT.
type=SYSTEM_SHUTDOWN msg=audit(1732290000.000:99999): pid=1 uid=0 auid=4294967295
subj=kernel msg='comm="systemd-shutdow" res=success'

description: The audit daemon started
sample:
Log Name:      audit/DAEMON
Source:        auditd
Event ID:      1200 (DAEMON_START)
Level:         Information
Host:          web01.prod.example.org
Description:
auditd itself came up and began writing records to /var/log/audit/audit.log.
type=DAEMON_START msg=audit(1732190000.100:2): op=start ver=3.1.2
format=enriched kernel=6.8.0-generic auid=4294967295 pid=612 subj=auditd res=success

description: The audit daemon stopped
sample:
Log Name:      audit/DAEMON
Source:        auditd
Event ID:      1201 (DAEMON_END)
Level:         Warning
Host:          web01.prod.example.org
Description:
auditd exited — either a clean shutdown/restart, or, if unexpected, a sign the
audit trail may have gaps. The Linux analogue of the Windows "Event log service
was stopped" condition.
type=DAEMON_END msg=audit(1732208900.200:50900): op=terminate auid=0 pid=612
subj=auditd res=success
reference: Cross-check against a planned maintenance window before treating this as benign.

description: The audit daemon aborted startup due to a configuration error
sample:
Log Name:      audit/DAEMON
Source:        auditd
Event ID:      1202 (DAEMON_ABORT)
Level:         Error
Host:          web01.prod.example.org
Description:
auditd failed to start because its configuration (auditd.conf or a rules file)
could not be parsed — the host is running with no active audit trail until fixed.
type=DAEMON_ABORT msg=audit(1732190005.000:3): auditd error halt=1 reason=RULE_LOAD
error_count=1 subj=auditd
reference: Check `journalctl -u auditd` and validate rules with `auditctl -R <file>` before restarting.

description: The audit daemon reloaded its configuration
sample:
Log Name:      audit/DAEMON
Source:        auditd
Event ID:      1203 (DAEMON_CONFIG)
Level:         Information
Host:          web01.prod.example.org
Description:
auditd re-read auditd.conf (e.g. after `service auditd reload` or a SIGHUP).
type=DAEMON_CONFIG msg=audit(1732209000.300:50950): op=reload-config auid=0
subj=auditd res=success

description: SELinux denied an operation (AVC denial)
sample:
Log Name:      audit/MAC
Source:        kernel (SELinux)
Event ID:      1400 (AVC)
Level:         Warning
Host:          web01.prod.example.org
Description:
A process was blocked from performing an operation its type enforcement policy
doesn't allow. Investigate whether this reflects a real intrusion attempt (a
process operating outside its expected profile) or a legitimate app needing a
policy update — `audit2allow -w -a` explains which.
type=AVC msg=audit(1732209500.400:51000): avc:  denied  { write } for  pid=22190
comm="httpd" name="shadow" dev="dm-0" ino=131099
scontext=system_u:system_r:httpd_t:s0
tcontext=system_u:object_r:shadow_t:s0 tclass=file permissive=0
reference: AVC is also the audit type AppArmor denials use — see the AppArmor AVC entry below.

description: AppArmor denied an operation
sample:
Log Name:      audit/MAC
Source:        kernel (AppArmor)
Event ID:      1400 (AVC)
Level:         Warning
Host:          bastion01.prod.example.org
Description:
AppArmor blocked an operation outside a confined process's profile. AppArmor
reuses the same AUDIT_AVC (1400) message type as SELinux — the two are told apart
by the message content (apparmor="..." vs avc: denied), not the type code.
type=AVC msg=audit(1732209600.500:51010): apparmor="DENIED" operation="open"
profile="/usr/sbin/nginx" name="/etc/shadow" pid=22301 comm="nginx"
requested_mask="r" denied_mask="r" fsuid=33 ouid=0
reference: aa-status shows loaded profiles and their mode; aa-logprof turns logged denials into profile updates.

description: The SELinux policy was (re)loaded
sample:
Log Name:      audit/MAC
Source:        semodule
Event ID:      1403 (MAC_POLICY_LOAD)
Level:         Notice
Host:          web01.prod.example.org
Description:
A new or updated SELinux policy was loaded into the kernel, e.g. via `semodule -i`.
type=MAC_POLICY_LOAD msg=audit(1732209700.600:51020): policy loaded auid=0
ses=4294967295 subj=unconfined_u:unconfined_r:unconfined_t:s0-s0:c0.c1023 res=1

description: SELinux enforcement mode was changed (enforcing ↔ permissive)
sample:
Log Name:      audit/MAC
Source:        setenforce
Event ID:      1404 (MAC_STATUS)
Level:         Critical
Host:          web01.prod.example.org
Description:
SELinux was switched from enforcing to permissive (or vice versa) — while
permissive, SELinux logs what it *would* have denied but blocks nothing, so this
is a high-value event to alert on outside a maintenance window.
type=MAC_STATUS msg=audit(1732209800.700:51030): enforcing=0 old_enforcing=1
auid=0 ses=12 subj=unconfined_u:unconfined_r:unconfined_t:s0-s0:c0.c1023 res=1

description: A netfilter (nftables/iptables) table was registered or replaced
sample:

Source:        kernel (netfilter)
Event ID:      1325 (NETFILTER_CFG)
Level:         Notice
Host:          web01.prod.example.org
Description:
The active firewall ruleset changed — a full table load/replace, e.g. from
`nft -f /etc/nftables.conf` or `iptables-restore`.
type=NETFILTER_CFG msg=audit(1732209900.800:51040): table=filter family=2
entries=48 op=register pid=910 subj=unconfined_u:unconfined_r:unconfined_t:s0-s0:c0.c1023
comm="nft"

description: A packet matched a logging firewall rule
sample:
Log Name:      audit/SYSCALL
Source:        kernel (netfilter)
Event ID:      1324 (NETFILTER_PKT)
Level:         Information
Host:          web01.prod.example.org
Description:
An individual packet was logged by a rule with the AUDIT (or nft `log`) target —
the Linux analogue of Windows Filtering Platform event 5157 "connection blocked".
type=NETFILTER_PKT msg=audit(1732210000.900:51050): mark=0 saddr=203.0.113.44
daddr=10.20.30.5 proto=6 sport=51422 dport=22 action=drop

description: Client-initiated disconnect after a normal session
sample:
Log Name:      ssh/protocol
Source:        sshd
Event ID:      11 (SSH_DISCONNECT_BY_APPLICATION)
Level:         Information
Host:          bastion01.prod.example.org
Description:
The client or server cleanly ended the SSH session — by far the most common
disconnect reason, logged with the numeric code straight from the SSH wire
protocol (RFC 4253).
Received disconnect from 203.0.113.44 port 54211:11: disconnected by user
reference: See the SSH disconnect reason codes reference table for the full set of 15 codes.

description: Malformed or out-of-sequence SSH packet received
sample:
Log Name:      ssh/protocol
Source:        sshd
Event ID:      2 (SSH_DISCONNECT_PROTOCOL_ERROR)
Level:         Warning
Host:          bastion01.prod.example.org
Description:
sshd rejected the connection because the peer sent an invalid or out-of-order
protocol message — normal for network scanners probing port 22, unusual from a
real SSH client.
Received disconnect from 198.51.100.23 port 41190:2: Too many authentication failures

description: All configured authentication methods were exhausted
sample:
Log Name:      ssh/protocol
Source:        sshd
Event ID:      14 (SSH_DISCONNECT_NO_MORE_AUTH_METHODS_AVAILABLE)
Level:         Warning
Host:          bastion01.prod.example.org
Description:
The client tried every authentication method sshd offered (e.g. publickey, then
password) without success — a classic brute-force / credential-stuffing signature
when it recurs rapidly from the same source.
Received disconnect from 192.0.2.15 port 33210:14: No more authentication methods
available
reference: Correlate with repeated USER_AUTH failures from the same addr= for the same window.

description: The SSH connection was lost at the network level
sample:
Log Name:      ssh/protocol
Source:        sshd
Event ID:      10 (SSH_DISCONNECT_CONNECTION_LOST)
Level:         Information
Host:          bastion02.prod.example.org
Description:
The TCP connection dropped without a clean SSH-level close — a flaky network path,
a client that crashed, or a firewall/NAT timeout, rather than either side
intentionally ending the session.
Connection reset by 10.20.30.5 port 60112 [preauth]

description: A unit's start job has begun execution

Level:         Information
Host:          web01.prod.example.org
Description:
systemd began starting a unit — the first half of a start job, paired with either
a "succeeded" or "failed" message once the job completes.
MESSAGE_ID=7d4958e842da4a758f6c1cdc7b36dcc5
UNIT=nginx.service
JOB_ID=482
JOB_TYPE=start

_PID=1

Host:          web01.prod.example.org

The unit reached the "active" state cleanly.
MESSAGE_ID=39f53479d3a045ac8e11786248231fbf

description: A unit's start job has failed
sample:
Log Name:      systemd/journal
Source:        systemd
Event ID:      be02cf68-55d2-428b-a40d-f7e9d022f03d
Level:         Error
Host:          db01.prod.example.org
Description:
A unit failed to reach the active state — the flagship "service failed to start"
event, worth alerting on for anything security- or availability-critical

UNIT=postgresql.service
JOB_ID=610
JOB_TYPE=start
JOB_RESULT=failed
_COMM=systemd
_PID=1
reference: `systemctl status <unit>` and `journalctl -u <unit>` for the underlying failure reason.

Level:         Error
Host:          db01.prod.example.org

A running unit exited unexpectedly (non-zero exit code, a crash, or a failed

UNIT=postgresql.service

description: A process was killed by the OOM killer
sample:
Log Name:      systemd/journal
Source:        systemd
Event ID:      fe6faa94-e777-4663-a0da-52717891d8ef
Level:         Warning
Host:          db01.prod.example.org
Description:
A process belonging to a unit was killed under memory pressure — by the classic
in-kernel OOM killer or by systemd-oomd — and systemd correlated the kill back to
the owning unit for this journal message.
MESSAGE_ID=fe6faa94e7774663a0da52717891d8ef
UNIT=postgresql.service
_COMM=systemd
_PID=1
reference: Follow up with `dmesg -T | grep -i 'killed process'` for the memory numbers at the time of the kill.

description: The system clock was changed
sample:
Log Name:      systemd/journal
Source:        systemd-timedated
Event ID:      c7a78707-9b35-4eaa-a9e7-7b371893cd27
Level:         Notice
Host:          web01.prod.example.org
Description:
The wall clock stepped — manually (date/timedatectl set-time), or via an NTP step
correction. A meaningful backward jump right after other suspicious activity is a
classic log-timeline-obfuscation signal, the Linux analogue of Windows Event ID
4616 "The system time was changed".
MESSAGE_ID=c7a787079b354eaaa9e77b371893cd27
_COMM=systemd-timedated
reference: Pair with an audit watch on /etc/adjtime and /etc/localtime to catch the configuration side too.

description: The journal service stopped
sample:

Source:        systemd-journald
Event ID:      d93fb3c9-c24d-451a-97ce-a615ce59c00b
Level:         Warning
Host:          web01.prod.example.org
Description:
systemd-journald exited — normal during a controlled shutdown/restart, but if it
happens mid-session it means logging has stopped on this host until it restarts.
MESSAGE_ID=d93fb3c9c24d451a97cea615ce59c00b
_COMM=systemd-journald
_PID=308

description: Log messages from a service were suppressed by rate limiting
sample:
Log Name:      systemd/journal
Source:        systemd-journald
Event ID:      a596d6fe-7bfa-4994-828e-72309e95d61e
Level:         Notice
Host:          web01.prod.example.org
Description:
A unit logged faster than journald's RateLimitIntervalSec=/RateLimitBurst=
threshold, so some of its messages were dropped — worth widening the rate limit
(or setting it to 0) for any unit whose every line matters for audit purposes.
MESSAGE_ID=a596d6fe7bfa4994828e72309e95d61e
UNIT=sshd.service
NUMBER_OF_MESSAGES_SUPPRESSED=214
_COMM=systemd-journald
